hn-50165801.t: Publish fake stats, get cited in LLMs
hn-50165801.s: How 50,000 fake stats kept getting cited by ChatGPT Read more on the Peec AI blog.
ex: What I learned about AI search when I made up 50,000 stats that got cited by ChatGPT... About 7 months ago, I launched a website with 50,000 statistics. Every one of them was fake. Google has forgotten the site exists and deindexed the pages, but ChatGPT hasn't. Since the website went live 7 months ago, it has sent more than 10,000 AI sessions its way. And now more than 330 referring domains, including Shopify, Bluehost, and DHL, link to the site. Its made-up numbers have also ended up in an academic paper and in a bank's investment research. At Peec AI and in the industry, we talk about GEO and SEO every day, and we keep looking for new tactics. I’ve been working on this stats page one for a long time, sharing pieces of it publicly along the way. Of course, it’s experimental, but the results have been hard to ignore.

hn-50169053.t: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
hn-50169053.s: This project provides a PyTorch backend for Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), enabling users to run PyTorch models and operations on TPU devices.
ex: This project provides a PyTorch backend for Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), enabling users to run PyTorch models and operations on TPU devices. It includes custom ATen kernels for various PyTorch operations, a compilation cache for optimizing execution, and examples for distributed training and model inference. PyTorch ATen kernel implementation for TPU. Compilation cache for optimized execution of XLA computations. Support for distributed training (Data Parallelism, Tensor Parallelism). Examples for various models (Llama, Qwen, ResNet, DLRM, minGPT, UNet). Integration with torch.compile() for graph mode execution. Utilities for debugging and benchmarking. A user guide is available at https://torchtpu.readthedocs.io/. This is a static version of the interactive notebooks. They are available in the docs folder. The notebooks are Marimo (similar to Jupyter). They can be run with marimo edit file.py and then you can access them in your browser.

hn-50165953.t: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust
hn-50165953.s: Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.
ex: Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain. Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser. To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that. The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation.

hn-50167286.t: VoidAccess – open-source dark web OSINT, from query to a graph
hn-50167286.s: Self-hosted dark web OSINT platform. Automated threat intelligence from query to graph in 13 steps. Free alternative to Recorded Future, DarkOwl, and Flare.
ex: Self-hostable OSINT for turning dark-web research queries into structured threat intelligence. Built for security researchers, threat-intelligence teams, and authorized investigators who need collection, enrichment, relationship mapping, and export in one workflow. - Parallel collection - searches Tor indexes, paste sites, code forges, security feeds, and curated .onion seeds. - Entity extraction - finds IOCs, wallets, credentials, handles, vulnerabilities, actors, malware, people, and organizations. - Multi-source enrichment - adds reputation, breach, passive DNS, sandbox, blockchain, and threat-feed context. - Actor intelligence - persists aliases, infrastructure, notes, timelines, and cross-investigation relationships. - Relationship graphs - builds co-occurrence graphs, communities, paths, and infrastructure clusters. - Content safety - filters prohibited queries, URLs, content, and extracted entities at mandatory pipeline gates.

hn-50167617.t: Jev Cards, Can you beat a vision model at a picture quiz?
hn-50167617.s: 100 picture cards: fruit, flags, maps, chess, illusions. Jev answers in about 0.3 s. Race it in Sprint, Versus or Streak.
ex: I built a quiz game around TypeSafe's new Jev model, which has vision capabilities. Jev looks at a picture and a question and picks an answer (or taps a place) in about a quarter of a second. I've always loved quiz games and thought this would be a fun way to see what it can do and how fast it is. I made the cards from scratch, and Jev gets exactly the picture you see. More cards will come over time. Play against Jev on your own (there's a leaderboard for each mode), or start a live match and challenge your friends, with Jev as one more player. The code is open source, so feel free to build your own game or make more cards that I can publish. Play: https://jevcards.com Code: https://github.com/Jose-Sabater/jevcards (the newest cards stay private for a while) Disclaimer: I ran Jev through both TypeSafe and Opper, and made the cards through Opper's vision models and Claude Code. I work at Opper, but jevcards is open source and free to play.

hn-50152466.t: Maxwell: A new kind of model that sits between code and hardware
hn-50152466.s: Maxwell improves code while it runs, adapting to hardware and data. Every improvement is formally proven equivalent to the original code.
ex: Maxwell understands and improves code while it runs, reasoning about hardware and data, not just code. Every improvement is formally proven equivalent to the original code. Read the manifesto → A short animated film, with narration and captions, introducing Maxwell: most code never sees the hardware it runs on or the data it processes. Maxwell watches a program while it runs, rewrites the binary underneath to fit that exact machine and data, and formally proves every improvement equivalent to the original. It runs on CPUs and GPUs, speeding up data pipelines and AI inference kernels. LTX built LTX-2.5 for efficiency from day one, compiled end to end, sequence-parallel across GPUs, decoding on a hand-written attention kernel. A pipeline built and optimized by top human experts. Maxwell made their 4K generation nearly twice as fast. Each run is labelled in the video. The original pipeline takes 4 minutes 9 seconds; with Maxwell, the same clip takes 2 minutes 14 seconds.

hn-50163502.t: AfD Leak: What 421,179 Hacked Emails Show about the German Far Right
hn-50163502.s: Hackers have published 281 GB of AfD emails as AI summaries, showing widespread antisemitism, racism, violent fantasies and alleged financial misconduct.
ex: A vast archive of hacked emails from the AfD was published online on Monday: 281 GB containing 421,179 internal party emails. And, for anyone who might have grown confused about claims of antisemitism while it was plastered over the German news media in the weeks following the Berlin election: here you can see what it really looks like. In email after email, party supporters use racist slurs and share antisemitic theories of Jewish world domination; there are jokes about turning refugees into handbags and boots, discussions of whether refugees should be shot at the border, a Christmas card sent with a swastika and “Heil Hitler”, and an email thread signed off with “Heil und Sieg”. HEIST is a worker-owned online magazine, founded by writers and editors who after years working across Berlin's media landscape believed something essential was missing. Anyone living here has felt a growing gap between the city as it actually is and the version being served up by mainstream outlets.

hn-50167583.t: Respan (YC W24) – Open-source Rust AI gateway built around plugins
hn-50167583.s: Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan ( https://www.respan.ai ). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers…
ex: Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan ( https://www.respan.ai ). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers, protocols (MCP, voice), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features (fallbacks, PII redaction, smart routing). Instead of packaging tons of providers and features into one gateway, Respan provides a small core and public interfaces that teams can use to assemble the AI infrastructure their application needs. That way, users can build their own features as additional plugins without having to change the gateway's core. Here’s a video demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVv2ibXiTXM There are countless LLM gateways and most of them solve a common problem: calling different providers from a single endpoint. However, adding new features can become prohibitively difficult. So developers can end up building another gateway to solve a specific problem.

hn-50170593.s: Build the city of your dreams. Subject to approval. A free city builder about zoning, hearings, lawsuits and reelection.
ex: You are the mayor. You know exactly what this city needs. Now get it past the zoning board, the neighbors, the appeals court and the next election. Permit Pending is a city simulation in the spirit of the classics, with one difference: you are not a god. You are an elected mayor. Every apartment block, bus lane and factory goes through hearings, reviews, objections, lawsuits and appeals. The economy underneath is real. The neighbors are not always rational. Win the argument, or win the election. Ideally both. A typical case from your inbox. The economic answer was obvious. The political path was not. New housing lowers rents and angers homeowners. New industry brings jobs and smog. Better transit attracts development, and development attracts opponents. Fix one problem and you create a new group of voters who are angry about it. Your inbox fills with applications, controversies and recurring characters.

hn-50166579.s: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream…
ex: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores. To demonstrate that the keys are compromised, the original reporter Wayne signed the following message with the private key of each of the eight intermediate CAs and reported it to the Root Program Teams on the 17th of October: proof.zip contains the message, and for each intermediate the certificate, its public key and a signature on the message. To verify with OpenSSL: The root programs and many downstream trust stores have taken action to protect their users. The certificates have been blocked in Firefox and Chrome since the 17th of October and in Apple devices since the 19th. The issue was responsibly disclosed to downstream trust stores on the 19th of October. Many have already released updates or are in the process of releasing updates.

hn-50165208.t: Apple broke an essential presentation feature of iPads
hn-50165208.s: If you teach or present with an iPad, avoid iPadOS 27.
ex: A brief digression from my usual teaching posts to complain about a devastating regression in iPadOS 27. If you’ve followed my work up until now, you’ll know that I rely heavily on writing on handouts from my iPad, projected via AirPlay to an external screen that my students can see. When I’m doing this, my iPad is also doing many other things: controlling a PowerPoint presentation on my Mac, showing me notes that I’ve taken on points I want to mention and students I want to call on, and showing me the results of polls before I reveal them to the class. This ability to do other things on your iPad while the audience just sees your presentation or handout is an essential part of a variety of pedagogical moves that I use in my teaching. As of iPadOS 27, if you have multiple windows open while AirPlaying (whether or not Stage Manager is on), tapping on anything other than the presenting app will snap the external display into showing your whole iPad screen.

hn-50169707.t: What shall I teach my son?
hn-50169707.s: Yesterday, the title The End of Education by Neil Postman called to me from my bookshelf, whispering that it might be the right book at the right time. It was.
ex: Yesterday, the title The End of Education by Neil Postman called to me from my bookshelf, whispering that it might be the right book at the right time. It was. Published in 1995, it was surprisingly appropriate balm for the soul of a confused programmer and soon-to-be father. My wife and I are expecting our first child. My economically valuable skillset – programming – suddenly feels less valuable. What shall I teach my son? And to what end? Mr. Edison says That the radio will supplant the teacher. Already one may learn languages by means Of Victrola records. The moving picture will visualize What the radio fails to get across. Teachers will be relegated to the backwoods. With fire-horses, And long-haired women; Or, perhaps shown in museums. Education will become a matter Of pressing the button. Perhaps I can get a position at the switchboard.

hn-50167028.s: Insofar as a political organization like Ofcom is even capable of admitting defeat, it did so in the 4chan enforcement today.
ex: Insofar as a political organization like Ofcom is even capable of admitting defeat, it did so in the 4chan enforcement today. In testimony before the Commons Digital, Culture, Media, and Sport Committee, Ofcom admitted it knows its jurisdiction ends where a foreign court’s jurisdiction begins. “If foreign courts decide to try and get in our way, there will be a point at which we have to accept that we won’t be able to recover that money.” Guido Fawkes characterizes this admission thus: “Ofcom Admits Defeat.” Guido is right. American courts have, by now, provided their preliminary view on the likelihood of Ofcom’s enforcement powers being successful in U.S. courts – the obiter dicta in 4chan v. Ofcom, the opinion in the case we filed against Ofcom in the federal District Court for the District of Columbia a little over a year ago.

hn-50166257.t: How I got over 300 Tor exit nodes removed
hn-50166257.s: On Friday Oct 2, 09:35am, 333 infected exit nodes started a coordinated campaign to intercept SSH connections and gather as much unencrypted data as possible.
ex: On Friday Oct 2, 09:35am, 333 infected exit nodes started a coordinated campaign to intercept SSH connections and gather as much unencrypted data as possible. To give you a sense of scale, all of Tor has around 3000 exit relays, so roughly 10% were under their control. The attackers had gained access to the servers two months earlier, in August, and quietly deployed their Ebury 1.8.3 payload (an OpenSSH backdoor and credential stealer for Linux). In this post I'll focus on the second attack, the SSH MITM. If you happen to get a circuit that exits over one of those 333 infected exit nodes, you won't notice anything at first. Encrypted web traffic is forwarded as usual, but if you attempt an SSH connection over Port 22, you're unknowingly redirected to one of 12 SSH interception servers. That's exactly what happened to me on Friday morning.

gh-1426240325.s: Prompts for you to use REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), get the most out of it, and clone or break down any program
ex: A curated collection of prompts for REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) — the toolset that lets your AI coding agent inspect how software works, from native binaries, firmware and kernels to games, Electron apps, APKs and websites. Prompts are ready to paste into your agent. Replace everything in and keep each request focused on one feature — narrow questions get evidence-backed answers. - REA tools & guides: https://rea.tools/ - Official prompt gallery: https://madewithrea.com/prompts - Intro thread ("REA is the most dangerous thing on the internet right now") by codila — https://x.com/0xCodila/status/2109623431763292649 (quoting Matthew Berman — https://x.com/MatthewBerman/status/2108245653843509415) 1. One feature per prompt. Broad "explain the whole app" questions return shallow maps; narrow ones return call chains and addresses. 2. Demand evidence. Every prompt here requires file/function/address citations — it stops the agent from confabulating. 3.

One Flexible Drafter for All Batch Sizes and Hardware Paper (EAGLE-4) · EAGLE-4 draft for Qwen3.8-27B · Documentation EAGLE-4 (Extrapolation Algorithm for Greater Language-model Efficiency) is the latest generation of the EAGLE family for accelerating large language model inference. One drafter adapts its speculative decoding strategy to the batch size, the hardware and the workload, and keeps the target model's output distribution. The EAGLE-4 draft uses a sliding-window draft layer, a low-rank candidate head and an append-only draft cache. Dense and latent-MoE draft structures are implemented. Qwen3.8-27B with its EAGLE-4 draft is the measured target pair. This repository is eagle-harness, a pip-installable package (eagleharness) that serves EAGLE-4 drafts on SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed through engine plugins. EAGLE-4 sizes the speculative tree from measured draft and verification costs for the batch size, hardware and workload it is running on.
